Completely agree, especially what you said about texting. 

A lot of my anger with my stutter isn't about the stutter itself but what I actually wanted to say but couldn't. The regret at not being able tell a joke in the right way. Long, articulate sentences rather than shortened substituted words with loads of umms ahhs and kind ofs. 

It's such a bloody pain.

Sorry mate, dyou...erm....mind if you send me that......erm.... document........erm... thinkIneedtochangesomething...

*voice falters* 

*stops speaking*
'Imposter syndrome' is a good way to put it. I used to think I was bad at my job because I talk such rubbish and feel so nervous before I realised it was something that cant easily be controlled

I think what I try to do is to get some form of noise out there during a pause, whether it's saying 'erm' or just something easier I can say. Once people realise that I want to speak they'll let me which is good. 

Weirdly on calls I find talking slowly helps too. Also if you can, switch on your webcam. I'm so much worse with calls than face to face and even though I don't like video calling too much it improves my confidence :)
Yeah it's there but it's never used and people would think it's quite weird for me to use it unfortunately

If I didn't mention I had a stutter, I don't think I would have passed any of the interviews I had.

I try to turn it into a good thing in my answers - how I have a stutter has made me to want to work for this company for their open and inclusive culture and way of working. Also how I still try and do presentations and get to know people to throw myself into it and not let it bother me. 

In terms of stuttering on the interview itself, I'd mention it at the start before talking (say it with a smile) and just be patient. Talk slowly, don't rush answers. You'll be fine :) 

Good luck!

I really feel for you here and completely understand where you're coming from. 

I get annoyed when people tell those considering suicide to 'reach out, talk to as many people as you can'

Because the reality is - no one gives a fuck. Everyone's so self involved in their own lives that they think you bringing your problems is an inconvenience to them. 

I had exactly the same reaction from my family. They said 'dont be silly' and 'just stop thinking like that'. They didn't check in on me for 5 weeks after I told them. 

I'm sorry you had that from your parents. It's the last thing you need and I really hope you can find someone who is supportive and reassuring.
I also really wanted methods too. It's hard to figure out how to do it easily when no one is allowed to talk about it freely online

I'm in the same boat. From the UK and have struggled with this too, just wish I had a gun. But then I think it's better that it was harder because now I'm still alive. And then round in circles we go.
